name: Dune Slip Face
description: The subject on the steep slip face of a dune at low sun, wind-carried grains streaming off the crest as a bright backlit smoke and ripple shadows raking across the frame in hard parallel bars. Graphic, dry and moving — the wind is visible rather than implied.
lighting: Low raking sun, long hard ripple shadows
subject: either
prompt: a low-profile sand-toned suede-and-mesh trail shoe with a gum-rubber outsole and a dark heel counter, the product is the hero of the frame and occupies roughly 50 percent of the frame width, tack-sharp and clearly lit, set on the steep slip face of a large sand dune at low sun, the slip face a clean avalanching plane of fine grain with real slump lobes and a shear line where the sand has slipped, the windward flank above it combed into regular wind ripples whose crests throw long hard-edged shadows raking across the frame in parallel bars, wind-carried grains streaming off the dune crest as a bright translucent smoke lit from behind that resolves into individual moving grains at its leading edge rather than reading as fog, a fine saltation haze skimming the surface at ankle height, low sun very close to the horizon and slightly behind camera-right so the ripples take maximum relief and the subject throws one long clean shadow down the slope, cool weak sky bounce as the only fill, warm gold and apricot on the lit sand against cool lavender-grey in every shadow with nothing muddy between them, a thin band of pale sky only where the crest line enters frame, the dune treated as supporting texture cropped tight at slope scale rather than shown as a wide desert landscape, genuine granular sand behaviour with a small displaced collar of grains where the subject has settled and loose grains resting on its upper surfaces, no footprints beyond the subject's own contact, no vehicle or animal tracks, no vegetation, no distant caravan or postcard desert silhouette, no sun disc in frame, no lens-flare stars, no second product, cinematic elemental realism
